key_insight: Long-link availability dominates slip-system activity, while an exponential link-length distribution filtered by threshold-like link velocities explains exponential stress dependence without thermal activation.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a microstructure-informed plastic flow rule for FCC single crystals that accounts for link-length distributions rather than relying on resolved shear stress alone.
method: Integrate length-resolved dislocation-link contributions using a generalized Orowan equation.
Represent average link velocity with a shared function of resolved shear stress and link length.
Capture most slip-system interaction effects through the link-length distribution.
evidence_signal: The model accurately reproduces DDD shear-rate data for all 12 slip systems across 99 loading orientations; rates span two orders of magnitude even within a narrow stress window.
watch_item: Practical use requires reliable link-length distributions; validation reported in the abstract is limited to FCC single-crystal DDD data.
paper_title: Plastic Flow Rule Based on Dislocation Link Velocity
